claims.text: The starting eutectic high-entropy alloy has a hierarchical microstructure composed of dual-phase lamellar colonies.
The untreated starting alloy has limited room-temperature tensile ductility and is brittle.
Phase-selective recrystallization can overcome limited room-temperature tensile ductility and brittleness while retaining or increasing strength.
The proposed phase-selective recrystallization treatment uses 800-1000°C for 1-2 hours.
The treatment targets optimization of lamellar-colony morphology and phase distribution.
Phase-selective recrystallization will refine the lamellar-colony morphology.
Phase-selective recrystallization will reduce dislocation density.
Phase-selective recrystallization will optimize phase distribution.
Phase-selective recrystallization reduces dislocation pile-ups near internal boundaries.
Reducing dislocation pile-ups near internal boundaries decreases local stress concentrations and microcracking.
Decreased local stress concentrations and microcracking enhance tensile ductility and reduce brittleness.
The untreated alloy has approximately 5% elongation at break.
The treatment will produce a 20-30% increase in tensile ductility.
The treated alloy will have 6.5-7.5% elongation at break.
The untreated alloy has a yield strength of approximately 800 MPa.
The treatment will increase yield strength by 10-20%, resulting in a yield strength of 880-960 MPa.
The predicted outcome applies to room-temperature tensile testing at a strain rate of 10^-3 s^-1.
The hypothesis is falsified if the treated alloy shows less than a 10% ductility increase or less than a 5% yield-strength increase relative to the untreated control.

contradictions.description: The stated ductility percentages are arithmetically inconsistent: increasing elongation from 5% to 6.5-7.5% corresponds to a 30-50% relative increase, not the claimed 20-30% increase.
